item: an emergency wipe in a folder the app does not own destroys only the app's files and says what it left (R711); wipe gaps rows 28-30, 35, 36
key_paths: src/safety/data_scope.py; src/safety/crypto_erase.py; src/safety/panic.py; src/safety/uninstall.py; src/api/unlock.py; src/static/data-volume.js; tests/test_data_scope.py; tests/test_crypto_erase.py; docs/SECURITY.md
summary: BEFORE: the erase walked and removed the whole data folder whatever it was, so OO_DATA_DIR set by hand to a home folder, a drive root or a projects folder meant the wipe (and the secure uninstall) overwrote and deleted the operator's own files. NOW (R711): ownership is where the app put the folder (the default location or the first-launch OOS data folder), never the app's files in it (session_state.json is written at every start, so a marker rule protected nothing: the security reads' first finding). A hand-set folder is shared when, on the path it leads to, it is the home folder, above it, a standard home folder, a drive root, a mount point, or holds any entry the app does not own (OS clutter aside; the scan stops at the first). There every by-name step still runs and the rest reaches only the app's own entries (names, side files, copy and staging patterns, atomic-write temps and lock sidecars; a test follows every name joined onto data_dir()); common names whose app contents say nothing about the corpus (cache, keys, leases, models, runtime) are left and named; a keys folder loses every key of the app's (named, *_ed25519.pem, *_ml_dsa_65.key, .pending) and keeps the rest; the folder is kept and the report names what was left (left_untouched, left_common_names, not_removed). The uninstall watcher applies the same names and logs only a count. Startup says it in the log, the terminal, and a notice on the unlock page and in the app (12 languages, a reason code, never the path). Row 28: lane pools close after their salt pages, so the close writes no log back first. Row 29: copies beside a database (salvage, damaged, pre-encrypt, in-progress encryption, pre-restore) are found wherever the database is; an encrypted store's lose their head and are unlinked before the slow rewrite, any other copy is rewritten whole. Row 30: the watcher keeps lane databases header-only. Row 35: a failing step after a completed erase is named in after_erase_failures instead of a 500. Row 36: kept descriptors are per wipe, so a second wipe never shortens the first one's late pass. Also: step 6 only head-overwrites and unlinks an encrypted store's database that step 1 could not unlink (Windows), instead of rewriting it whole. Stated limit: databases (corpus, custody, wiki.db, law.db, osm.db) are erased by name in either scope. Release line: The emergency wipe and the secure uninstall no longer delete your own files when the app's data folder is a folder you share with them (a home folder, a drive, a projects folder): they destroy the app's files, keep yours, say what was left, and the app warns about such a folder at every start.
